info.name: MASAR API
info.description:
Clean, professional Postman collection for the MASAR backend, built directly from `routes/auth.php`, `routes/users.php`, `routes/api.php`, and the actual controllers/validators.

Base URL variable: `{{base_url}}` (default `http://localhost/masar-backend`).

## Suggested flow
1. **00 - Environment / Setup -> Health Check** to confirm the backend is reachable.
2. **01 - Authentication**: Register, then Login. Login captures `access_token`, `user_id`, `user_role`, `csrf_token` and the HttpOnly `refresh_token` cookie automatically.
3. **02 - Users**: authenticated account endpoints (Bearer token + CSRF header handled by pre-request scripts).
4. **03 - Auth & Users Security Tests**: run after the happy-path requests to verify error handling.

## Test credentials
All credentials are safe development placeholders (`@test.local`). Set them to accounts that actually exist in your environment (for example the seeded dev accounts `admin@masar.test / Admin@123456`, `student@masar.test / Student@123456`, `company@masar.test / Company@123456`) before running the Login requests.

## Authentication notes
- Protected endpoints use `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}`.
- Token refresh uses the server-issued HttpOnly `refresh_token` cookie (path `/api/v1/auth`) plus the `X-CSRF-Token` header, which must match the `csrf_token` cookie. The collection attaches the CSRF header automatically from the cookie jar.
- CSRF-protected write endpoints (`PUT /users/me`, `DELETE /users/me`, `POST /auth/refresh`) require a prior successful Login so the CSRF cookie exists.
- There is currently no routed email-verification endpoint in the backend, so it is intentionally omitted.
- reCAPTCHA is disabled in the local `.env` (`RECAPTCHA_ENABLED=false`), so `recaptcha_token` is not required. If enabled, add it to the register/login/reset bodies.

item.name: Login & Session

request.description: Public. Authenticates a user. On 200 the response returns `data.token` (access token) and the server sets an HttpOnly `refresh_token` cookie plus a readable `csrf_token` cookie. The test stores all of these in collection variables. Set `{{student_email}}`/`{{student_password}}` to an account that exists in your environment.
Public. Logs in a company account. Expected: 200 when approved, 403 when the company registration is pending/rejected.

exec: pm.test("Company login succeeds or reports pending approval", function () {

request.description: Public. Logs in an admin account. Expected: 200.
Requires Bearer token. Returns the currently authenticated user from the token identity.

Requires the HttpOnly `refresh_token` cookie and a matching `X-CSRF-Token` header (attached automatically by the pre-request script). Run after Login. On 200 the server returns a new access token and rotates the refresh/CSRF cookies.

exec: pm.test("Refresh succeeds and returns a new access token", function () {

request.description: Requires Bearer token. Changes the authenticated user's password. On success all tokens are revoked and cookies cleared, so re-login is required afterwards.

Requires Bearer token. Revokes the current session tokens and clears the refresh cookie. The test saves the used access token into `revoked_token` so the security tests can verify a revoked token is rejected.

item.description: Login and session lifecycle. Login captures tokens; Refresh rotates them; Logout revokes them.

item.name: Password Reset

request.description: Public. Requests a 6-digit password reset OTP for the email. The OTP is delivered by email (never in the response); paste it into the `reset_token` collection variable. The response is generic so account existence is not revealed.

exec: pm.test("Password reset OTP request succeeds", function () {

Public. Verifies the reset OTP for the given email before allowing the password reset. Expected: 200 when the OTP is valid.
Public. Resets the password using the verified OTP. The account password becomes `{{new_password}}` and all tokens are revoked.

item.name: Google OAuth

request.description: Public. Generates a Google authorization URL. The backend creates a single-use server-side state (expires in 600s) and embeds it in the URL. The test stores the returned URL and extracts `state` into `google_state`. Open the URL in a real browser to obtain the authorization `code`.

Public. Exchanges the Google authorization code for a session. Requires a real `code` (obtained by opening the authorization URL from the Start request in a browser) and the matching single-use `state`. The backend validates and consumes the state server-side, then redirects to the frontend. Redirect following is disabled so the redirect is visible. If the Google email has no account, one is auto-created as a student and a welcome email is sent.

exec: pm.test("Google callback returns a MASAR auth response", function () {

item.description: Google OAuth. The Start request is fully scriptable; the Callback requires a real browser step (the Google authorization `code`).

Every authentication endpoint implemented in `routes/auth.php`. Protected requests carry `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}`; the refresh flow uses the HttpOnly refresh cookie plus the CSRF header.
